items.t: What if a nation turns back to God?
items.d: What if a nation turns back to God? Jeremiah shows that repentance matters even when judgment has been pronounced.
p: God warns before judgment, and a nation that turns from evil can receive mercy instead of the destruction it was headed toward.

Clip · Saving a Nation What if a nation turns back to God? Jeremiah shows that repentance matters even when judgment has been pronounced. God warns before judgment, and a nation that turns from evil can receive mercy instead of the destruction it was headed toward. Jeremiah 18:8; Jeremiah 12:17 — “If that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, says the LORD.” Jeremiah 18:8 says, “If that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it.” Pastor David G. Kincer explains that God warns before judgment and that turning from evil to Bible morality brings a people under His protection. If that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, says the LORD. — Jeremiah 18:8; Jeremiah 12:17 (NKJV) Jeremiah 18:8; Jeremiah 12:17 (NKJV) — “If that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, says the LORD.” Plain language: hear God’s Word, turn from evil, and let Scripture do its work in your life and community. Jeremiah 18:8 says, “If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” Pastor Kincer says God warns before He judges. If a nation turns from its evil ways and back to Bible morality, God can relent from the judgment He planned. If that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, says the LORD.

items.t: Can a divided home still stand?
items.d: Can a divided home still stand? Jesus said a house divided against itself shall not stand.
p: A husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by example, or the home will not stand.

Clip · Division Part 1 Can a divided home still stand? Jesus said a house divided against itself shall not stand. A husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by example, or the home will not stand. Matthew 12:25 — “But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: ‘Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.’” Jesus said, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand” (Matthew 12:25). Pastor David G. Kincer says husband and wife must stand together in the same truth and show their children Jesus by their lives, or the home will not stand. But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.” — Matthew 12:25 (NKJV) Matthew 12:25 (NKJV) — “But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: ‘Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.’” Plain language: let God’s Word unite us, keep Christ at the center, and live out the same truth together. Jesus said every kingdom, city and house divided against itself shall not stand (Matthew 12:25). Pastor Kincer says “stand” is a military word: an army that isn’t united loses the war. In the home, husband and wife must stand together with the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go two different ways, conflict comes, and the kids can’t wait to get out. But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.”

items.t: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
items.d: Do we want God’s blessings and approval without letting God rule our lives? Scripture asks us to choose whether His Word will govern us.
p: We may want heaven and God’s blessings, but God wants to rule in our lives through His Scriptures.

Clip · Saving a Nation Do we want God’s blessings and approval without letting God rule our lives? Scripture asks us to choose whether His Word will govern us. We may want heaven and God’s blessings, but God wants to rule in our lives through His Scriptures. 1 Samuel 8:7; Luke 19:14 — “They have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them” and “We will not have this man to reign over us.” Israel wanted to do what was right in its own eyes. When the people rejected Samuel, God said they had rejected Him — not merely His prophet. The same warning appears in Jesus’ parable: citizens wanted the benefits of a kingdom, but refused the king’s rule. They have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them. We will not have this man to reign over us. — 1 Samuel 8:7 · Luke 19:14 1 Samuel 8:7 (NKJV) — “They have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.” Luke 19:14 (NKJV) — “But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We will not have this man to reign over us.’” Plain language: don’t ask only for God’s blessings and approval. Let God and His Scriptures rule in your life. They rejected God, rejected the Scriptures, and did what they wanted in their own eyes. People want to go to heaven and want His blessings, but do not want to do what He tells them to do. Luke 19:14 says, “We will not have this man to reign over us.” People want God’s blessings and approval, but God wants to rule in their life — and He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life. They have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them. We will not have this man to reign over us.

items.t: Does “be perfect” mean never fail?
items.d: When Jesus says “be perfect,” He isn’t demanding a flawless life — He’s calling you into spiritual maturity and completeness.
p: “Be perfect” means grow into maturity — not never mess up.

Clip · A More Excellent Way When Jesus says “be perfect,” He isn’t demanding a flawless life — He’s calling you into spiritual maturity and completeness. “Be perfect” means grow into maturity — not never mess up. Matthew 5:48; James 1:4 — Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. … that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. Jesus said, “Therefore you shall be perfect.” A lot of people hear that and shut down — “You can’t be perfect; we all sin.” They thought perfect meant a life with no flaws. Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. — Matthew 5:48 No — it means spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness. James 1:4: let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. God is taking His people somewhere. Ask yourself: Am I growing up — or staying a spiritual child? Matthew 5:48 — Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. James 1:4 — But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. Hebrews 5:14 — But solid food belongs to those who are of full age… Plain language: “perfect” here means mature and complete — not never mess up. Grow up. Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. … that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.

items.t: What if my gifts are just noise?
items.d: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love — I’m just noise. A clanging cymbal.
p: Speech without love is just noise — a clanging cymbal. Love is the more excellent way.

Clip · A More Excellent Way Watch on YouTube Shorts ↗ Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love — I’m just noise. A clanging cymbal. Speech without love is just noise — a clanging cymbal. Love is the more excellent way. 1 Corinthians 13:1 — Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. In A More Excellent Way , Pastor David G. Kincer opens 1 Corinthians 13 where Paul left off in chapter 12: desire the best gifts… and I will show you a more excellent way. Then Paul says: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. — 1 Corinthians 13:1 Languages of people. Languages of angels. Impressive. But without love, Paul says it’s worthless racket — the kind of noise that makes you cover your ears and ask, “What’s the point?” Love isn’t the soft add-on after the gifts. Love is the more excellent way. Ask yourself: Am I impressive — or am I loving? 1 Corinthians 12:31 — But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way. 1 Corinthians 13:1 — Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. Plain language: giftedness without love is empty noise. Love is the more excellent way Paul points to. Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.

items.t: Does real love insist on its own way?
items.d: Love doesn’t say “my way or the highway.” Love … does not seek its own, … thinks no evil.
tg: love does not demand its own way
p: Love … does not seek its own, … thinks no evil.

Clip · A More Excellent Way Love doesn’t say “my way or the highway.” Love … does not seek its own, … thinks no evil. Love … does not seek its own, … thinks no evil. 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 — Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Paul doesn’t leave love vague. In 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 he defines it — patient, kind, not proud, not rude — and then the line that lands at home and church: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. — 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 Love does not demand its own way in the family, the church, or the community. It demands the right way — the truth. And it isn’t touchy; it keeps no ledger of hurts. Ask yourself: Am I demanding my way — or the right way? 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 — Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Plain language: love won’t bully the room into “my way,” and it won’t keep score of wrongs. Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

items.t: Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?
items.d: You can prophesy, cast out demons, and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still hear Him say, “I never knew you.”
p: Being used by God is not the same as being known by Him; gifts without love still hear “I never knew you.”

items.t: What is the real goal of God’s Word?
items.d: The goal of the commandment is love out of a pure heart. Gifts and religious activity are means — not the destination.
p: Worship, prayer, and gifts are means — love from a pure heart is the goal.

Paul sums it up in 1 Timothy 1:5. The word purpose means the goal . Paul says the goal is love — and God distributes gifts as He wills. Gifts are means. Love is the goal. items.t: Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?
items.d: Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of divine character. Don’t chase manifestations without becoming like God.
p: Character (love) comes before chasing spiritual fireworks.
